candidates.qualitative_priority: medium-high after a useful real-GPU trace
candidates.hypothesis_or_question: The cuDNN GRU path has dispatch/layout/alignment choices that matter for our sequence and batch shape.
evidence: E525 backward is 404.99 ms in the local profile.
PyTorch/cuDNN docs expose version/device/layout-dependent recurrent algorithms; PyTorch's specific documented persistent condition names V100, so it must not be assumed on T4.

If dispatch demonstrates a Tensor Core alignment fallback, test zero-extension of H230 input width 211 to the smallest installed-version multiple (e.g. 216 for an 8-wide rule or 212 for a 4-wide rule), preserving the original input matrix with zero extra columns; require forward/state/reset, gradient and one optimizer-step parity before matched full-step timing. Test only one layout/alignment/kernel change at a time.
candidates.falsifier: Candidate dispatch is unsupported or adds copies/launches and fails to beat whole-step wall time.

candidates.qualitative_priority: conditional; only if trace shows host-launch gaps
candidates.hypothesis_or_question: Static-shape capture/fusion reduces CPU launch and pointwise overhead enough to reduce end-to-end time.
evidence: PyTorch reduce-overhead mode may use CUDA Graphs but can use more device memory and may not capture.
Current H230 CUDA event and host waits overlap; event/wall ratio is not utilization.
candidates.cheapest_discriminating_test: Start with a no-fit capture feasibility/parity probe, then compare full-profile startup+steady-state wall and memory against eager; retain compile time and graph recapture counts.
candidates.falsifier: No capture, graph breaks, numerical/optimizer-clock drift, memory pressure or amortized wall regression.

candidates.hypothesis_or_question: A larger physical batch or microbatch accumulation can increase examples processed per useful GPU second.
evidence: Compact E522 B16->B32 was +1.94% throughput with +81.94% observed VRAM and different target/model; not an H230 effect.
candidates.cheapest_discriminating_test: Resource profile first, then frozen paired recipes with the same effective examples/update, loss denominator, optimizer/scheduler/EMA clocks and step budget; report fixed endpoint separately.
candidates.falsifier: Throughput gain is offset by memory or the matched quality endpoint falls.

candidates.qualitative_priority: scientifically distinct; promising if cost-per-quality matters
candidates.hypothesis_or_question: Longer causal gradient flow across recurrent chunks improves the fixed endpoint enough to justify extra backward cost.
evidence: Trainer exposes chunk, macro update_rows and detach_rows separately; detach_rows is the gradient horizon, while update_rows determines optimizer cadence.
Truncated state is still carried causally across the sequence.
candidates.cheapest_discriminating_test: Choose one common update_rows macrostep that allows both candidate detach schedules; compare detach_rows values with same inputs, update count, batch order, clipping, scheduler, EMA, seed pairs and complete official endpoint.
candidates.falsifier: Longer horizon raises compute/memory without a repeatable useful endpoint/teacher contribution, or state/reset/gradient parity fails.

candidates.qualitative_priority: conditional compute-for-capacity component when activation memory constrains a wider teacher or longer tested gradient horizon
candidates.hypothesis_or_question: Checkpointing recurrent chunk computations during backward may lower peak activation memory enough to test longer temporal credit assignment or a larger teacher, at an unknown recompute-time cost.
evidence: PyTorch documents that checkpointed segments are replayed during backward; non-reentrant mode supports autograd.grad and detached tensors in the region, while RNG stashing/replay can add overhead.
The original sublinear-memory work includes long recurrent-sequence examples, but no effect was measured for this model/trainer.
The trainer separates detach_rows (gradient horizon) from update_rows (optimizer cadence); changing them remains a scientific treatment.
candidates.cheapest_discriminating_test: At one frozen detach/update horizon, wrap the exact recurrent chunk forward returning logits and carried state with torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint(..., use_reentrant=False); keep the existing autocast context identical on recompute (use context_fn only if required). Check forward/state/reset, input/parameter gradients, successful GradScaler step, checkpoint reload, peak GPU memory and full backward wall. If valid and memory falls, test a longer detach_rows horizon with and without rematerialization under the same update_rows, examples, optimizer/scheduler/EMA clocks and official fixed endpoint.
candidates.falsifier: No meaningful peak-memory reduction; checkpoint recomputation changes forward/state/gradient/update behavior; recompute makes full fit less useful than available capacity alternatives; or the paired longer-horizon endpoint provides no useful value at its measured cost. These outcomes apply to the tested boundary, not all checkpoint placements.
candidates.mechanism_family: activation memory and temporal credit assignment
dependencies: source inspection of actual recurrent chunk/carry/autocast boundary
fresh resource gate and paired recipe review before any science fit

candidates.falsifier: No wall-time benefit, overflow/scale instability, unacceptable gradient or prediction drift, or downstream student endpoint worsens.

candidates.qualitative_priority: conditional high-value input-path probe if matched traces confirm repeated parquet decode/materialization is on the critical path
candidates.hypothesis_or_question: A hash-bound row-major mmap of the existing exact float32 features could amortize repeated Arrow row-group decoding and column-stack/transpose materialization across epochs or same-source fits, without increasing loader workers.
evidence: Local H230 measured loader wait 418.46ms versus 1095.08ms outer-batch wall, with near-zero H2D; intervals overlap so wait is not a separate wall component.

Owned SequenceFile.read selects a full sequence row group and 112 feature columns, stacks and materializes a contiguous row-major float32 array; the raw feature payload is 8.96MB/sequence. Sequences.__getitem__ calls it on each sampled item.
Two DataLoader workers already hit the scoped 5GB RAM cap on the compact E522 probe; replacing decode/copy work may be safer than increasing workers, but this is not measured.
candidates.cheapest_discriminating_test: Only if actual exact-shape trace confirms input wait matters, compare the current reader with one source-hash-bound row-major float32 feature mmap generated through SequenceFile.read. Require bitwise feature/target/mask and row-order/split identity. Measure one-time build and incremental transfer, cold and warm epoch times, loader wait, storage and anonymous/file/page-cache RAM; leave workers at zero. Compute the measured break-even `T_build + K*T_cached < K*T_parquet` for actual planned passes/fits.
candidates.falsifier: Reader is not on the critical path; build/staging/storage cost exceeds saved read time for the authorized number of passes; cache identity/order differs; or resource ceilings are violated.
dependencies: source identity and existing reader parity
